experiment: d=5 rotated (XZZX-form) surface code, 4 rounds of stabilizer measurement, X basis (Bluvstein et al., arXiv:2506.20661, Fig. 2; Nature 649, 39-46 (2025))
clock: t_start_us is on the Moving-AWG clock, t=0 at SEGMENT[4] ("### Start of circuit"). Other AWGs are placed by a single constant offset each, fitted so that their 16 CZ anchors coincide with the 16 Moving-AWG Wait[10 us] slots (residuals below). SEGMENT[1] loops until the trigger (t_start_us=null); SEGMENT[2] is placed back-to-back before t=0; SEGMENT[6] (readout) is placed at the end of the Raman string (end of the bright-state transfer) -- an assumption, its trigger time is not given.
maps_to_tick_definition: index of the TICK-delimited layer of circuit-qec.stim containing the realized operation: 0 = data preparation, 1/3/5/7 = QEC rounds 1-4, 2/4/6 = empty layers between the double TICKs, 8 = final data rotation + measurement. The published file has only 8 TICKs (no per-CZ TICK); stim_lines gives the exact line(s) of circuit-qec.stim (1-based).

paper_round_time.quote: In the repeated surface code experiments in Figure 2, each QEC round was 4.45 ms. This originated from 0.47 ms time between gates, and a total of 2.57 ms from moving the ancilla atoms to the storage zone and bringing in the next group to the entangling zone.

totals.reconciliation: Moving AWG: rounds 2-4 are each exactly 4450 us = 4 x 470 us (0.195 ms move + 10 us CZ hold + 0.195 ms move + 70 us local-gate hold) + 2570 us exchange (1250 us return of the used block: 0.1+0.4+0.4+0.1+0.25 ms; 1250 us pick-up of the next block: 0.25+0.1+0.4+0.4+0.1 ms; one 70 us hold before the first CZ). This reproduces the paper (4 x 0.47 + 2.57 = 4.45 ms). Rydberg AWG: 4 x (Pulse + Wait[467.800 us]) + Wait[2570.02 us] = 4450.02 us with the inferred 2.2 us pulse segment. Raman AWG: 4449.164 us between round markers of rounds 2-3 (0.84 us short; individual CZ periods are 467.784 / 471.784 us, i.e. up to +-1.8 us local slip against the 470 us Moving period; the Raman string is one phase-continuous waveform). Raman AOD AWG: 4449.80 us. Round 1 differs by construction: the first ancilla block is brought in before the circuit (SEGMENT[2]) and round 1 begins with the data pi/2, fake ancilla pi/2 and a 76 us global echo instead of a pick-up. Text notes inside the command string disagree with its own durations: "Exchanging the ancilla arrays is currently given 1 ms total time" (commands: 2 x 1.25 ms), "Move data back to storage zone, 1.2 ms" (commands: 1.85 ms), "SSR on half, 1.2 ms" / "1.23 ms" (commands: 2.1 / 1.9 ms incl. waits).
totals.stim_idle_model: original-noisy.stim idles 2 x 235 us per CZ gap (= 470 us) and 2 x 1285 us per block exchange (= 2570 us), i.e. 3 x 470 + 2 x 235 + 2 x 1285 = 4450 us per round: the noise model uses exactly the hardware timing (verify.txt).

entangling.data_sites: data (r,c) at x = 16 + 3c, y = 2 + 2r (inferred: data occupy x tones 1..5 of xd_ent=COMB[13,3,6] and y tones 0..4 of yd_ent=COMB[2,2,6])
entangling.ancilla_home: ancilla at plaquette centre (ra,ca) sits at x = 16.36 + 3ca, y = 2 + 2ra (xanc_ent=COMB[14.86,3,6], yanc_ent=COMB[1,2,6]); during a CZ layer the whole ancilla grid is shifted by SHIFT[[dx],[dy]]
quotes: The 420-nm and 1013-nm Rydberg tophat beams cover 7 rows of gate sites in the entangling zone and are homogenized to ≈ 1% peak-to-peak variation over a vertical extent of 60 μm.
The entangling zone is separated by 40 μm from the storage and readout zone (overlapping in these measurements) to ensure negligible error on stored qubits from the tails of the Rydberg beams.

storage_and_readout.note: storage and readout zones overlap in the surface-code experiments; each atom row has a second trap row 1 SLM unit (4.9 um) below/above it for spin-to-position readout (SSR moves shift dark atoms by dy=-1)

block_x_offsets_slm.ancilla_block_5_unused: not addressed in the command string

storage_and_readout.block_x_formula: x = x_st[k] + offset, x_st = COMB[-0.98,3,6] (6 tones, pitch 3 SLM = 13.8 um): six blocks interlaced column-by-column
quotes: For surface code experiments (Figs. 1-3), the same static traps are used for mid-circuit storage of ancilla blocks and for readout of all qubits at the end of the computation. The readout zone is 12 rows tall (55 μm) with two rows of traps per atom for the lattice readout, Fig. 2a. Six blocks of qubits are interlaced horizontally for storage, corresponding to five (four) 6x6 ancilla blocks and one (two) 5x5 data block(s) in Fig. 2(3).
Two additional columns of traps form a small reservoir used for initial rearrangement, resulting in a total array width of 165 μm.

moving.preamble_prose_verbatim: The command string used to program the RF waveforms for the Moving AWG, which control the positions and powers of moveable AOD tweezers, is given below. Waveforms are uploaded to different segments of the AWG using the SEGMENT[] command, which can then be individually looped or triggered with an external trigger. Each move is defined using a MOVEAOD command. The initial position and power is specified for the first command when tweezers are turned on. For subsequent commands, the arguments specify where to move to (and optionally the power to ramp to), and take the form MOVEAOD[[x_positions, y_positions],([xpowers,ypowers],) time_for_move]. Additional arguments such as SHIFT apply a global (x,y) coordinate shift to the coordinates in that move. Coordinates are given in 'SLM units' where 1 SLM unit here is approximately 4.6um in the x direction and 4.9um in the y direction (corresponding to 7 and 7.5 units in the corresponding Supplementary Video, respectively)

raman.preamble_prose_verbatim: The command string used to program the I/Q waveforms and AOM amplitudes for local and global Raman control is given below. The command specifies the parameters for each single‐qubit gate, which is then converted into the appropriate waveforms to modulate the light intensity and microwave phase and frequency (defined relative to the resonance frequency). For local gates, the pulses are optionally gated on and off by the Raman AOD command. Examples of typical commands are Z : global Z rotation, in units of 2*pi E : wait time, idling at the specified frequency SC1_ECHO : global SCROFULOUS Y(pi) pulse for dynamical decoupling, idling at the specified frequency SC1_H_FIXEDLOOPED_SMOOTH_PCOMP : SCROFULOUS Y(pi/2) local gaussian pulses SC1PI_FIXEDLOOPED_SMOOTH_PCOMP : SCROFULOUS Y(pi) local gaussian pulses BB1_FIXED: global BB1 pulse
